catalog_quote: Estes dados ilustram que, na língua juruna, o acento ocorre sempre na última sílaba das palavras e/ou em sílaba de tom alto : pelos exemplos (162) a (167), observa-se que o acento cai sempre em sílaba de tom alto, e que, pelos exemplos (164) e (165), tal sílaba deve ser sempre a primeira da esquerda para a direita a apresentar tom alto; pelos exemplos (168) a (170) nota-se que,caso não haja tons altos, o acento cai na última sílaba da palavra. Assim, poderia ser postulado o seguinte algoritmo para o acento na palavra : "O acento ocorre na primeira sílaba a partir da esquerda, que apresenta tom alto. Caso não haja sílaba com tom alto, o acento ocorre na última sílaba". Contudo, o exemplo (169) contraria isso por apresentar acento na última sílaba, que apresenta tom alto. Tal exemplo não constitui exceção [...] Diante desses dados e de vários outros, o algoritmo anterior deve ser modifica…
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Yudja (juru1256) is not in the catalog. The single searched title, Fargetti 1993 'O peso silábico na análise do acento em Jurúna', is about Yudja word stress but could not be obtained: the author's own 2001 bibliography lists it as an unpublished manuscript ('m.s'), while Fabre's record (copied by Glottolog) attaches to it the GEL-anais venue of her other 1993 paper 'Considerações sobre acento e tom em Jurúna'; neither is online (GEL archive starts 2011; no S2/OpenAlex/Crossref record). Priority low, because thesis fn. 14 (p. 82) states that sec. 1.3 of Fargetti 2001 supersedes both 1993 texts. Best first-hand statement read: Fargetti 2001 thesis pp. 83-84 (held by the project) -- stress on the leftmost high-toned syllable, final when all tones are alike; stress predictable, tone contrastive; sec. 1.3.6 adds a Hayes-style metrical reanalysis where syllable weight (CVC/CVV) matters in slow speech and tone prevails in fast speech. The 1992 dissertation (sec. 3.7, p. 111) states the same rule. Also downloaded: Fabre's Tupi dictionary file (record source) and Fargetti 2006 orthography article (silent on placement).

new_statements.quote: Estes dados ilustram que, na língua juruna, o acento ocorre sempre na última sílaba das palavras e/ou em sílaba de tom alto [...] Diante desses dados e de vários outros, o algoritmo anterior deve ser modificado : ''Ocorre acento na primeira sílaba com tom alto da esquerda para a direita. Caso todos os tons sejam iguais, o acento recai sobre a última sílaba.'' Ou seja, na ausência de tons altos na palavra, ou numa seqüência de tons iguais (altos ou baixos), o acento recai sobre a última sílaba. [p.84:] Portanto, conclui-se que o acento é predizível, não possuindo "status fonológico", e que o fator condicionante da ocorrência do acento nas várias posições é o tom.
new_statements.translation: These data show that in Juruna stress always falls on the last syllable of words and/or on a high-toned syllable [...] Given these data and several others, the earlier algorithm must be modified: 'Stress falls on the first high-toned syllable counting from left to right. If all the tones are the same, stress falls on the last syllable.' That is, when the word has no high tones, or in a sequence of identical tones (high or low), stress falls on the final syllable. [p.84:] It is therefore concluded that stress is predictable, having no 'phonological status', and that the factor conditioning where stress occurs is tone.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Juruna is a two-tone (H/L) register-tone language; word stress is non-contrastive and predictable from tone: primary stress goes on the leftmost H-toned syllable of the word; if the word's syllables all bear the same tone (all L or all H), stress is word-final (default-to-opposite-edge unbounded system: 'first H, else last'). Fargetti's later metrical formalisation (sec. 1.3.6, pp.93-98): quantity-sensitive unbounded right-headed feet ((C)VV and word-final glottal-closed syllables heavy), tonal prominence H>L projected onto foot heads, End Rule Left.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described; fn.16 (p.87) states Juruna has unbounded stress and no bounded feet, and no secondary/rhythmic stress is mentioned anywhere in sec. 1.3.
new_statements.exceptions: Apparent minimal stress pairs (exx. 152-161, e.g. [paku'a] 'banana' vs [pa'kúá] 'pacuzinho') are reanalysed as tone pairs. Syllable weight (long vowels, final [ʔ]) interacts with stress mainly in slow speech; 'em fala rápida, o tom prepondera' (p.98); ex. [kaːra'ʔiʔ] has stress on the final glottal-closed syllable rather than the initial CVV. In song the tonic can shift (karuka: final stress in isolation, initial in the melody, p.90).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level rule stated over isolated words in phonetic transcription (citation forms); p.90 explicitly contrasts stress 'na palavra fora do contexto da melodia' with sung forms. Tone, not stress, is the lexically contrastive suprasegmental; the orthography marks neither, Fargetti's transcription marks H tone.
new_statements.identity_note: Fargetti describes Juruna (autonym Yudjá) as spoken in the Parque Indígena do Xingu, Mato Grosso (aldeias Tubatuba, Pixayã, Kuni, Akã etc.), i.e. the language juru1256 itself; no dialect division is made. She notes the sister language Xipaya separately (not covered by the stress rule).

Ou seja, na ausência de tons altos na palavra, ou numa seqüência de tons iguais (altos ou baixos), o acento recai sobre a última sílaba. [p. 83] Portanto, conclui-se que o acento é predizível, não possuindo "status fonológico", e que o fator condicionante da ocorrência do acento nas várias posições é o tom. [p. 84]
new_statements.translation: In view of these data and many others, the previous algorithm must be modified: 'Stress occurs on the first high-toned syllable from left to right. If all tones are the same, stress falls on the last syllable.' That is, in the absence of high tones in the word, or in a sequence of identical tones (high or low), stress falls on the last syllable. [p. 83] Therefore, stress is predictable, having no 'phonological status', and the factor conditioning the occurrence of stress in its various positions is tone. [p. 84]

new_statements.reading: Yudja is a tone language with predictable, tone-driven word stress: stress lands on the leftmost H-toned syllable; when the word has uniform tone (no H, or all H) stress is final. In the 2001 metrical reanalysis (sec. 1.3.6) this is modelled as unbounded, right-headed, quantity-sensitive feet (CVC with glottal coda and CVV heavy; CV light) with an End Rule decided by tonal prominence; weight effects surface mainly in slow speech while 'em fala rápida, o tom prepondera' (p. 99). For catalog purposes: not fixed-position; stress predictable from tone (leftmost H), default final; the 1992 dissertation gives the same rule.
